title: Best B2B outreach software: how to choose the right fit for your sales team
content_html:
The best B2B outreach software is the one that fits how your sales team already finds, contacts and follows up with business buyers. For many small teams an off-the-shelf outreach tool is enough. Teams with an unusual sales process or strict rules on customer data may need software built around that process instead.

What is B2B outreach software?

B2B (business-to-business) outreach software helps a sales team contact potential business customers in an organised way. It replaces loose lists, scattered notes and memory with one place where the team plans and tracks outreach.

The choice matters because outreach touches two things a business cares about: the relationship with buyers and the customer data behind it. A tool that does not fit your process gets worked around. A tool that handles data in ways you have not checked creates risk.

What are the main options?

There are four broad types of options. Each one suits a different kind of team.

OptionWhat it isWho it suits
Off-the-shelf outreach toolA ready-made software package you sign up for and configureTeams whose sales process matches how the tool is set up
What your current CRM already offersContact and follow-up features inside the CRM you already use, where your CRM has themTeams that want fewer tools and already keep customer data in one CRM
Ready-made product from a software companyA product built for outreach by a company that also builds custom software, such as Reach from Upward TechnologiesTeams that want a product to start from, with the option of custom work around it
Custom-built softwareOutreach software designed around your own process, built by an agency or by your own IT teamTeams with an unusual process, specific data rules or many systems that must connect

Off-the-shelf tools. This is often the fastest way to start. If the tool fits your process, buying it is usually the sensible choice. You do not need custom software for a problem a package already covers.

Your existing CRM. Before you add a new tool, check what the CRM you already pay for can do. One less tool means one less place for customer data to live.

A ready-made product from a software company. This sits between buying and building. You start from an existing product and can ask the same company for custom work where your process differs.

Custom-built software. This makes sense when packages almost fit but not quite and the gaps cost your team real effort. It needs more thought up front, so it should start with a clear scope.

How to choose the best B2B outreach software

Work through these questions before you compare any tools:

  • Does it fit your process? Write down how your team finds leads, makes first contact and follows up. Then check each option against that list, not against a feature sheet.
  • What should stay personal? Some steps work well automated and others need a real person. Our article on what to automate and what to keep personal in B2B outreach goes through this in detail.
  • Does it connect to the systems you already use? Outreach data is most useful when it reaches your CRM and ERP without being typed in again. See how to integrate ERP and CRM so data enters once for how that works.
  • Where does customer data go? Read each vendor's terms on how it stores and processes your data. Ask for a processing agreement where GDPR (the EU privacy rules) applies to your outreach.
  • Who hosts and supports it? Find out who keeps the software running, who updates it and who you call when something breaks.
  • What does it cost in total? Compare the full cost over time, including every user and every extra tool you would need next to it.

If an option passes all of these, you have found your fit. If none of them do, that is the point where custom software becomes worth a look.
